messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Increased P99 latency + container restarts observed in continuous-batcher svc (us-west-2). Paging threshold crossed. Auto-page to eng-oncall.

Aisha: saw this spike ~3m ago. dashboards show sustained P99 > 6s and OOMs on batcher pods. Multiple restarts on node ip-10-0-3-21.

Ben: on it. are customers impacted?

Aisha: yeah, a handful of real-time endpoints (search-suggester) hit timeouts. Support already flagged 2 customers.

Clara: logs show repeated `cuda runtime: out of memory` inside worker loop, plus long GC pauses on the host. snippet: ```
2026-03-15T09:11:03Z batcher[pid=3124] ERROR: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
2026-03-15T09:11:03Z container restart
```

Ivan: node flapped (kubelet went NotReady) around same time. suspect OOM + memory pressure causing eviction.

Aisha: root cause hypothesis: continuous-batcher prefetch growth + an odd request pattern caused unbounded batch accumulation -> GPU memory spike.

runtime-bot: Runbook: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/continuous-batcher#gpu-oom (referencing mitigation steps).

Ben: quick mitigation plan: 1) reduce prefetch/backpressure window 2) disable aggressive prefetch on affected deployment 3) shift traffic to fallback model pool 4) cordon+drain hotspot node if it keeps flapping.

Clara: I can flip a feature flag to reduce prefetch from 512 to 64. suggest ENV `CB_MAX_PREFETCH=64` and `CB_BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS=30` as emergency values.

Aisha: +1. push a canary to one replica first. keep one pod with original config for comparison.

Ben: doing traffic shift now: routing 40% -> fallback-model (cpu) via router rule. command: ```./infractl route update --service batcher --split 60,40 --targets primary,fallback```

ops-bot: Deploy started by Ben: deploy/batcher-config-emer-20260315 (id: d-0a1b)

Clara: canary flipped. attaching the env change: ```kubectl set env deploy/batcher DEPLOY_ENV=prod CB_MAX_PREFETCH=64 CB_BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS=30 --record```

Ivan: cordoning node ip-10-0-3-21 now: `kubectl cordon ip-10-0-3-21` then `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — draining in progress. one pod failed to terminate cleanly, force restarted.

Aisha: after config change + traffic shift P99 dropped from 6.2s -> 1.0s on canary cluster. OOMs stopped on those pods. looks promising.

Ben: monitoring for 10m. can we also check kernel OOM logs on the flapping node? `dmesg | grep -i oom` and `journalctl -u kubelet`

Clara: saw many allocations pinned to batch accumulation in our logs. also spotted `std::bad_alloc` in one worker thread before the cuda error. could be host-side fragmentation.

runtime-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-20260315-221 (link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-20260315-221). Priority: P1 - customer-facing latency spikes.

Aisha: customer comms: drafted short note for support. will post to status page if we hold.

Ben: thumbs up. continuing to watch. if any OOMs reappear -> scale down batcher replicas and force model fallback.

Ivan: after draining the node, kube rescheduled affected pods to healthier nodes. no further kubelet NotReady events.

Clara: post-mortem notes to capture: - continuous-batcher lacked hard cap on in-memory prefetch queue - kernel memory fragmentation amplified GPU OOMs - no automatic graceful degradation path from GPU->CPU fallback under memory pressure.

Aisha: items for follow-up (triage): 1) implement hard cap env `CB_HARD_QUEUE_LIMIT` + enforcement 2) add automated fallback when GPU memory crosses threshold 3) add node-level memory pressure alert to prevent kubelet OOM evictions 4) replay harness to reproduce thundering prefetch pattern.

Ben: assigning owners: Clara -> config caps + canary test, Ivan -> node pressure alerts, Aisha -> customer comms & postmortem writeup, runtime team (cc @runtime) -> automated GPU->CPU fallback.

ops-bot: Note: rollback available: previous config (cb-max-prefetch=512) saved as cfg-20260314. Use `infractl deploy rollback cfg-20260314` if needed.

Clara: will open PR for `CB_HARD_QUEUE_LIMIT` and add a validation in admission controller to reject values > 256 by default.

Aisha: after 25m monitoring, system stable. P99 holding ~1.1s and no more restarts. marking mitigation success for now.

Ben: great work team. we'll run full postmortem tomorrow. leaving this thread open for additional follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
